examples.title: A marketing page with 19 planted accessibility bugs
examples.prompt: Audit this landing page for accessibility and fix everything serious.
examples.summary: A SaaS landing page built the way generated UIs often are: clickable divs, outline:none, placeholder-only fields, a newsletter form that traps Tab, a hover-only menu, a cookie bar that hides focused controls. axe-core plus the keyboard pass flag 20 rules (4 critical, 12 serious) and rank them in a Fix first list. The fixed twin, with semantic HTML, visible focus and real labels, comes back with 0 issues across 29 focus stops.
examples.result: 4 critical · 12 serious · 4 moderate → 0 on the fixed twin

media.alt: Annotated screenshot of the Brightly landing page: solid orange boxes mark axe findings (image-alt, color-contrast, placeholder-label, select-name), dashed boxes mark keyboard-pass findings (kbd-unreachable nav items and feature cards, kbd-hover-only on Resources, kbd-focus-trap in the footer form), and magenta numbered badges show focus stops with no visible focus.
media.caption: Before: solid boxes are axe findings, dashed boxes are keyboard-pass findings. Magenta badges are focus stops with no visible focus ring, and their numbers jump around because of a positive tabindex.

media.alt: Annotated screenshot of the fixed Brightly page: no issue boxes, only blue focus-order badges on the nav, hero buttons, cards, labelled form fields and footer.
media.caption: After: the fixed twin. No issue boxes, and every focus stop is blue, meaning a visible focus indicator was measured.

examples.excerpt:
## Fix first

Highest impact first, then by how many elements one fix touches (fix the shared component or token once).

1. `image-alt` (critical, 2 elements): Images must have alternative text
2. `select-name` (critical, 2 elements): Select element must have an accessible name
3. `button-name` (critical, 1 element): Buttons must have discernible text
4. `kbd-focus-trap` (critical, 1 element): Keyboard focus is trapped
5. `kbd-focus-not-visible` (serious, 12 elements): Focused element shows no visible focus indicator
6. `kbd-unreachable` (serious, 8 elements): Clickable element cannot be reached with the keyboard
7. `color-contrast` (serious, 5 elements): Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds
8. `placeholder-label` (serious, 4 elements): Form field is labelled only by its placeholder

examples.title: A subscription signup form that only looks finished
examples.prompt: Check our checkout signup form for accessibility problems and fix them.
examples.summary: A coffee-subscription signup shown right after a failed submit. The audit flags 7 fields named only by a placeholder, a light-red error message and a grey password hint that fail contrast, two custom checkboxes with no focus ring, and a 'Continue to payment' div that Tab never reaches. contrast.mjs gives the nearest passing shade of each color. Two planted bugs are not machine-checkable: the postcode error shown only as a red border, and errors not linked to their fields with aria-describedby. Those are left for the human review step, and the fixed twin fixes all six and passes clean.
examples.result: 4 serious rules on 12 elements → 0 on the fixed twin

media.alt: Annotated screenshot of the Oatfield Coffee signup form: every text field boxed as placeholder-label, the red error text and grey password hint boxed as color-contrast, the two custom checkboxes marked with magenta badges for no visible focus, and the Continue to payment bar dashed as kbd-unreachable.
media.caption: Before: placeholder-only fields, two contrast failures, checkboxes with no focus ring (magenta badges 11 and 12), and a div submit button the keyboard can't reach.

media.alt: Annotated screenshot of the fixed signup form: visible labels above every field, error messages with an icon in darker red under the email and postcode fields, a darker password hint, and 14 blue focus badges ending on a real Continue to payment button.
media.caption: After: visible labels, errors as text and icon tied to the field, the colors contrast.mjs suggested (#7e7570 hint, #cf474c errors), a focus ring on the checkbox, and a real button as stop 14.

examples.title: An app shell whose modals leak focus and ignore Escape
examples.prompt: Make the inbox nav and the New ticket modal keyboard accessible.
examples.summary: A support-desk inbox with a hover-only Reports menu and two hand-rolled modals, audited with --state to open each one. In the New ticket modal, Tab walks through 12 inbox controls hidden behind the backdrop, reported as focus leaking out of the open modal (kbd-focus-outside-modal), and Escape does nothing. The Keyboard shortcuts modal closes on Escape but drops focus to <body> instead of its button. With a disclosure button for the menu and native <dialog> with showModal() for both modals, all three states pass.

media.alt: Annotated screenshot of the Kitebird inbox with the New ticket modal open: focus badges 1 to 12 sit on the New ticket button, Bulk actions, filter chips and ticket links behind the dimmed backdrop, each dashed and labelled kbd-focus-outside-modal, before badges 13 to 19 reach the modal's own controls.
media.caption: State 1 (after clicking New ticket): focus stays on the trigger, and the first 12 Tab stops are inbox controls behind the open modal's backdrop. The modal's own fields only come at stops 13 to 19.

media.alt: Annotated screenshot of the fixed New ticket dialog: six blue focus badges, all inside the dialog, from Customer email to Create ticket.
media.caption: Fixed: native <dialog> with showModal(). Focus starts on the autofocused email field, Tab stays inside, Escape closes the dialog and focus returns to New ticket.

media.alt: Top bar of the Kitebird inbox with focus badges on each tab and the Reports tab boxed with a dashed kbd-hover-only label.
media.caption: Base page: hovering Reports opens a 3-link submenu, but focusing it does not, so kbd-hover-only.

examples.excerpt:
1. `kbd-focus-outside-modal` (serious, 12 elements, 1 page): Focus leaves the open modal for the page hidden behind it
2. `kbd-hover-only` (serious, 1 element, 1 page): Menu opens on mouse hover but not from the keyboard
3. `kbd-dialog-escape` (moderate, 1 element, 1 page): Escape does not close the open modal dialog (ARIA APG dialog pattern)
4. `kbd-dialog-focus-return` (moderate, 1 element, 1 page): Closing the dialog does not return focus to its trigger
